summary: csv-cleaner now passes clean. All five findings from the v1 review are resolved: the api.cleanmycsv.io call is named in the description, explained in the new Workflow step 3, and registered in references/external-calls.json with what data it sends and why (F1); the description is now 68 words with an explicit when-to-use cue and mentions both the overwrite behavior and the external call (F2); the script writes to <path>.cleaned.csv by default and only overwrites the original when the user explicitly asks via --in-place, removing the irreversible-by-default risk (F3); the orphaned references/legacy_notes.md was deleted since it documented an abandoned approach with no bearing on the current implementation (F4); and the overwrite/backup instruction is now two separate, clearly-worded Workflow steps (F5). The one remaining gate-mode candidate — 'Bash' declared but not referenced by name — was checked against the real body and dismissed as a false positive: the tool is genuinely needed to run both scripts/clean.py and curl, the check just can't see that from a literal name search.
